videos.script: Every night at two, the office's files should be copied to a backup. Nobody is at the office at two. Something on the server has to start the copy by itself, at the right time, whether or not anybody logged in that day. {{night}} Most of what a computer runs is like that: programs nobody started by hand. The print queue, the clock synchronisation, the update check, the backup. Lesson 1 called them services, started by the first process when the machine boots. {{services}} This lesson is about controlling them. Which ones are running, and which ones start at boot. How to stop one, and how to make sure it stays stopped. And how to make a task run on a schedule. {{control}} You will do it on Linux with systemctl and a timer you write yourself. You will see the older cron doing the same job. Then you will meet the Windows names, Services and Task Scheduler, and the Mac's, launchd. {{steps}} The transcripts come from lesson 3's server. The Windows and macOS commands are shown, not run. {{honest}}
